comment: Numeric ratchet manifest (DR-27a). Two arrays, two directions, one mechanism — tests/guards/numeric-floor-manifest.test.ts enforces both. `floors` entries may RISE, never fall. `ceilings` entries may be LOWERED, never raised: a budget or a maximum that can be raised to fit whatever the artifact grew into is not a budget, it asserts that the current size is the current size. Each entry pins a value AND the number of sites spelling it: the guard requires at least `occurrences` matches of `pattern` in `sourceFile`, so moving one site out of several is caught. New entries are allowed in either array; move `floor`/`ceiling`, `pattern` and `occurrences` together, and only in the permitted direction. Equality baselines (the GIT_MD_* / SKILL_* / TOTAL_* constants in tests/goldens/github-status-lines.test.ts) ratchet in neither direction and are not registered here.

floors.description: Number of compiled MDS host commands in dist/commands/ (MDS_COMMAND_HOSTS). The discovery assertion is a set-equality against tests/fixtures/mds-manifest.ts and this floor is that manifest's length, asserted alongside the set: the set says WHICH hosts, the floor says the roster may not shrink behind it. The pattern names its RECEIVER because partial-count in the same file now pins the same number: two entries sharing one bare pattern have no per-entry accounting, and the decrement probe of each would keep finding the other's site.

Number of .mds partial files anywhere under src/ (ALL_MDS_PARTIALS = MDS_PARTIALS under src/assets/commands/_partials/, plus MDS_REFERENCE_PARTIALS elsewhere). The discovery assertion is a set-equality against tests/fixtures/mds-manifest.ts over a repo-wide walk that classifies by the build's own rule -- no output-dir: key -- so a partial parked outside _partials/ is named rather than merely counted; this floor is its length. Floors rise with the roster, never fall — a partial deleted rather than inlined takes its callers with it silently.

DIST_FILES count = COMMAND_HOSTS (13) + release.md (1); DIST_FILES vs COMMAND_HOSTS divergence is permanent (SG-13). Five sites spell it, including the `<!-- devflow:` marker negative guard, which asserts both the built file count and its own distFilesScanned counter — the value is one number and the occurrence count is what stops one site drifting out of the set.

Minimum timeout in ms for the slow shell-exec tests that spawn scripts/build-mds.ts. Three sites, all negative-path spawns in this file: two dest-safety refusals and the ignored-dir walk. Every other isolated MDS build routes through buildCommittedTree(), whose own timeout is pinned by the mds-build-spawn-timeout-ms entry below.

Minimum timeout in ms for runMdsBuild() — the one spawn site every isolated MDS build now routes through, including buildCommittedTree(). Same floor as slow-test-timeout-ms, in the file the sites moved to.
Minimum number of subagent_type literal sites across dist+scripts corpus (currently ~66+)
MAX_CHARTER_CHARS = 75% of the 4096-char shell injection cap; orchestrator charter must stay at or below this
Minimum number of DEVFLOW_PLUGINS registry entries
Minimum install-path references in dist/commands/ files

D11 forward guard: posting ops (--body-file / -F body=@) that must reference Comment-sink scrub (D11), counted over the sink corpus gitAgentSinkCorpus() returns -- the resolved Git agent UNIONED with dist/skills/git/references/*.md, sliced in extractOpSection mode 'union' [DR-18]. The union is load-bearing: posting mechanics live in the generated references, so a git.md-only count would drop below the floor for reasons that are not a regression. The plugin-count entry above pins a different >= 8 in a different file.

resolveAllAgents() size — every DEVFLOW_PLUGINS agent resolves through the shared resolver (AC-0.7, GAP-07). 17 includes the hook-spawned Tracker agent, which is declared in devflow-core-skills.agents and filtered at install time rather than held outside the roster. A floor may only rise.
Operations indexed from git.md by the seam test's op→section map [DR-24]
Operations with at least one live caller fence. Directions 1 and 2 iterate this map; if it empties, both pass vacuously (the defect this floor exists to make loud).

KEYS in issue_capture_contract() checked by the seam test's producer direction. Six: the three original keys plus ISSUE_ID, ISSUE_PR_LINK and ISSUE_BRANCH_TOKEN, whose producers are the `### Handoff Values` block setup-task and fetch-issue emit. ISSUE_URL has no producer in git.md and is deliberately out. The direction is checked PER PRODUCER OP rather than over a concatenation, so it ranges over more (key, op) pairs than there are keys; the key count is what this floor pins.

The 60 000-character body cap, asserted at 7 sites in tests/git-agent.test.ts: the manage-debt archive threshold, the post-wave-report cap, each summary op's positive union assertion plus its known-bad probe that the literal is NOT reachable once the PR-host tree is dropped (both summary operations' compose steps live in the PR-host references), and the containment negative arm's in-scope witness that its scanned surface reaches the compose templates. The pattern is a substring of the negated form too, which is why the probes count; lowering the cap at any one site is caught.
D10 dedup-marker guard: two >= 2 floors in git-agent.test.ts (post-review-summary and post-resolution-summary dedup markers); lowering either site is caught

AC-0.10 containment guard (issue-body): ops wrapping remote issue content in <untrusted-issue-body> — setup-task, fetch-issue, fetch-issues-batch. The pattern names this entry's id so it matches ONE site: the sibling containment-external-thread-floor pins the same value 3 in the same file, and a bare toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(3) at occurrences 2 is satisfied by the pair jointly, each entry's count met by the OTHER entry's assertion with neither site individually accounted for (PF-018).

AC-0.10 containment guard (external-thread): ops carrying <external-thread> for review thread bodies — fetch-review-threads, post-resolution-summary, post-wave-report. Pattern narrowed to this entry's own site for the reason recorded on the sibling containment-issue-body-floor entry above: two entries sharing one pattern in one file have no per-entry accounting.

BUILD/TARBALL SCOPE: the manifest the build EMITS, which is every provider plus the provider-independent trees. Distinct from installed-reference-count-{github,provider}, which pin what ONE install carries; the build stays complete so the tarball can serve any selection without a rebuild, and narrowing the install never lowers this floor. 42 = 10 GitHub ops + 10 Jira ops + 10 Linear ops (the SAME TRACKER_OPS roster, which is what makes file-set parity structural) + 8 PR-host ops (PR_HOST_OPS, under no provider: pull requests stay on GitHub whatever the tracker is) + 3 cross-cutting documents + the tool-call contract, whose generation gate the first tool-call provider opens. Two sites — the manifest shape assertion and the 0644 normalisation's installed-file count. A manifest short enough to enumerate by hand makes every convergence assertion vacuous (GAP-42/PF-018), which is the same reason MIN_VARIANT_PAIRS exists. A floor may only rise, and here it rises by a whole module at a time.

GAP-15 forwarding seam: Code-agent spawn sites carrying an ISSUE_NUMBER key across implement.md (9, including the parallel-strategy pr-create spawn #359 added) and dynamic-build.md (6). The relational assertion -- every ISSUE_NUMBER payload also carries ISSUE_PR_LINK -- is vacuous over an empty or truncated payload set, so the site count is the non-vacuity floor and may only rise as spawn sites are added.

BUILD/TARBALL SCOPE (unaffected by the selection-scoped install): prefix-shippability clause (i) — the tarball must carry every file the reference overlay converges to. The floor keeps the packed-set assertion non-vacuous if the manifest is ever narrowed. It pins the same manifest as generated-reference-manifest-size at the OTHER sink, and the two must move together, or a module could ship un-packed.

Total `**Process:**` / `### Process` blocks in the tracker corpus (dist/agents/git.md + the generated reference tree). The corpus split is asserted by provenance as well as by count: git.md's own contribution is 18, so a bare 18 was met with the generated tree entirely absent while the guard claimed to scan both (PF-018). 57 = 18 in git.md + 1 learn-conventions + 30 provider blocks (ten per-op references for each of the three providers) + 8 PR-host blocks. A provider adds its whole roster at once, so the floor moves by a module rather than by a file.

Minimum characters a generated tracker reference must carry, owned by tests/tracker/reference-floor.ts and imported by the three suites that measure that shape one step apart: reference-reachability.test.ts (the GitHub tree), linear-module.test.ts (the Linear tree) and jira-module.test.ts (the Jira tree plus the `@define` body the generator reads). One owner because a number spelled at each site can drift at one of them while every other site and a presence-only guard stay green. Registered as a FLOOR, not a ceiling: every assertion reading it is `content.length < MIN_REFERENCE_CHARS` → problem, so raising it makes all three suites stricter, while LOWERING it is the weakening move — it re-admits the shape the constant exists to catch, a reference that kept its heading and lost its body. Its own JSDoc names it a floor.

Column-0 `## ` lines the live generated reference tree must carry INSIDE a code fence, so the PF-063 structure guard's absence assertion is exercised against real fenced headings rather than a corpus that has none. Today: manage-debt.md's `## Items` (1) plus ensure-traceable-issue.md's heredoc and D3-template headings (6). Lowering it re-admits a corpus in which fence-awareness is proven only by the synthetic probes in tests/guards/agent-source-resolver.test.ts.

Rows HOSTILE_PAYLOADS must carry — seven register payloads, each targeting a different sink (command substitution in two spellings, flag injection, line injection, size, credential-in-URL, query-operator escape), plus the two identity payloads that are the only rows exercising `## Assignee`'s second prohibition. Registered as a FLOOR because the payload grid grades every row against every schema cell: a row ADDED widens the evidence and must never cost a suite failure, while a row REMOVED narrows the sinks the grid covers with nothing else reporting it. Spelled as an exact count it was the ratchet inverted — adding a payload, the thing a reviewer most wants a contributor to do, failed the suite.

Rows HOSTILE_REFS must carry — shell separator, command substitution, both flag-injection spellings, path traversal, size, the zero-numbered key an unanchored digit class admits, and whitespace. Every pinned grammar in PROVIDER_REF_GRAMMARS is driven over the whole table, so one row added widens the corpus for every provider at once and one removed silently narrows it for all of them. A FLOOR for the same reason as min-hostile-payloads.

Distinct devflow: skill references across the widened closure corpus (dist/commands + agent sources + skill bodies incl. references/). Non-vacuity floor for the bidirectional requires: guard — a scanner that stopped matching would make both arms pass over an empty corpus. Measured 2026-09-19: 200 files, 297 sites, 44 distinct.

Reference files ONE github install carries: the tracker/github tree, the provider-independent PR-host tree (pr/, 8 files) and the cross-cutting documents. Install-time scope, distinct from the build-time floor, which is unchanged — the build still emits every provider so the tarball can serve any selection without a rebuild. Re-derived 2026-09-22 when the PR-host tree landed: 21 files.

Reference files ONE jira or linear install carries: the github floor (21, which already includes the 8 provider-independent PR-host files) + the selected provider's own 11. Excludes tracker/_mcp.md from the count assertion path, which is asserted biconditionally instead. Install-time scope, distinct from the build-time floor. Re-derived 2026-09-22: 32 files.

AC-0.6b: REQUIRED_OPS detected as doing remote I/O, over git.md UNIONED with the PR-host references (the corpus #326's move made necessary — a git.md-only read silently narrows the set to 13 because post-resolution-summary's gh indicators all moved with its body). Replaces a bare `> 0` non-vacuity check, which one detected op satisfies and which therefore cannot tell a corpus narrowing from a real removal. Zero headroom at 14: the D4 evidence half of the same guard stays git.md-only (PF-027 — a degradation clause a spawn can decline to load is not a contract), so the two halves read different corpora on purpose.

ceilings.description: THE git.md ceiling — the one gate on dist/agents/git.md, the always-loaded half of the tracker contract/mechanics split and a term every loaded-set row below carries. Re-derived by #360 as a measured 42_850 ch plus the RESERVATION LEDGER (2,050 ch since #360, PR2, spent its 150-ch line; one line per future PR of the SDLC-evidence series #357): PR3b 250 · PR4 900 · PR5 900. The reserved headroom is spoken for, not slack: each PR in the series spends only its own line, and any addition outside the ledger funds itself with a cut. The measurement follows #326's move of the eight PR-host operations' bodies into references/pr/{op}.md and #358's moves of non-contract text into the references each operation already loads, plus the condensed ## Principles, then #359's and #360's fixes. No per-component decomposition of any cut is recorded — three successive re-derivations of such components disagreed once already (PF-057) — so measure the artifact instead: npm run build && node -e "process.stdout.write(String(require('fs').readFileSync('dist/agents/git.md','utf8').length))". May be LOWERED, never raised: a budget raised to fit the artifact is not a budget, it asserts that the current size is the current size.

Max characters of the worst-case tracker spawn under the JIRA provider — its own row, never folded into budget-loaded-set. The GitHub row keeps bytes(tracker/_mcp.md) = 0 BY CONSTRUCTION, so pricing a provider that DOES load the contract on that row would bill every GitHub user for bytes they never receive (GAP-02), and would do it by raising a ratcheted ceiling. Re-derived by #360 as a measured 74_312 (shape '2-jira. per-op split, jira path') plus the RESERVATION LEDGER (2,050 ch since #360, PR2, spent its 150-ch line; one line per future PR of the SDLC-evidence series #357): PR3b 250 · PR4 900 · PR5 900. The reserved headroom is spoken for, not slack: each PR in the series spends only its own line, and any addition outside the ledger funds itself with a cut. git.md growth lands in every loaded-set row, so this row reserves the whole ledger. Re-measure rather than trust a figure restated here: npm run build && npx vitest run tests/tracker/byte-budget.test.ts prints every row. Trimming references/tracker/_mcp.md is the sanctioned first response to this row going red (contract prose, and the single largest term this row adds over the GitHub one), condensing the jira mechanics the second; neither is 'give the provider more room'. budget-loaded-set-linear is the sibling row; a registered MCP-backed provider with no such entry fails a named arm in the same file. LOWERED, NEVER RAISED.

Max characters of the worst-case tracker spawn under the LINEAR provider — its own row, for the reason the jira row is one (D-LOADED-SET-PER-PROVIDER). Re-derived by #360 as a measured 76_271 (shape '2-linear. per-op split, linear path') plus the RESERVATION LEDGER (2,050 ch since #360, PR2, spent its 150-ch line; one line per future PR of the SDLC-evidence series #357): PR3b 250 · PR4 900 · PR5 900. The reserved headroom is spoken for, not slack: each PR in the series spends only its own line, and any addition outside the ledger funds itself with a cut. git.md growth lands in every loaded-set row, so this row reserves the whole ledger. Re-measure rather than trust a figure restated here: npm run build && npx vitest run tests/tracker/byte-budget.test.ts prints every row. This is the LARGEST of the four rows, and its max_op is the largest of the three providers' for a recorded reason rather than by accident: backlink-shipped-issues is where the dedup ladder is stated, and on a stock official server three of its four rungs are unreachable (OD-12), so each rung's unavailability plus both halves of the rank-4 marker predicate have to be written down. LOWERED, NEVER RAISED.

Max characters of src/assets/skills/git/SKILL.md, derived at design time from the pre-split capture of that file less the projected cut, and pinned to that derivation rather than re-derived from whatever the file measures today. The skill carries doctrine, not mechanics: anything that grows it back past this is mechanics that belong in a generated reference. May be LOWERED, never raised.

Max characters of the worst-case tracker spawn on the GITHUB path, where bytes(tracker/_mcp.md) is 0 by construction (no github op file names the contract; the re-scoped AC-2.7 arm in tests/guards/provider-scope.test.ts proves it, and a gate in the same file repeats the check against every github mechanics file). Re-derived by #360 as a measured 64_016 (shape '2. per-op split, GitHub path') plus the RESERVATION LEDGER (2,050 ch since #360, PR2, spent its 150-ch line; one line per future PR of the SDLC-evidence series #357): PR3b 250 · PR4 900 · PR5 900. The reserved headroom is spoken for, not slack: each PR in the series spends only its own line, and any addition outside the ledger funds itself with a cut. git.md growth lands in every loaded-set row, so this row reserves the whole ledger. Re-measure rather than trust a figure restated here: npm run build && npx vitest run tests/tracker/byte-budget.test.ts prints every row. LOWERED, NEVER RAISED: the sanctioned response to it going red is moving text out of the agent or condensing the github mechanics.

Max characters of the worst-case spawn that runs one of the eight operations whose mechanics live under references/pr/ — its own row, for the reason each provider has one (D-LOADED-SET-PER-PROVIDER). references/pr/ is installed under EVERY tracker, because pull requests, PR reviews and PR checks stay on GitHub whatever issues the project files elsewhere, so a PR operation costs the same bytes on all three paths: folding it into the per-provider rows would price one cost three times while answering nowhere the question a reader asks (what does a PR spawn load?), and it cannot ride the GitHub row, which is scoped to TRACKER ops by D-LOADED-SET-SCOPE. The formula is the preloaded set plus max over PR_HOST_OPS of ( chars(references/pr/{op}.md) + every reference that op's own section names ); no max_op term of its own, because an op's PR-host file is already inside its one-spawn load and a separate largest-file term would count it twice. ONE WRITTEN EXCLUSION, references/github-api.md, declared as LOADED_SET_WRITTEN_EXCLUSIONS in tests/tracker/budget-model.ts: two of these ops loaded it long before any split existed, #326 moved the line that names it without changing a byte a spawn pays, and charging 21_355 ch of it here would bury the pr/ bodies this row exists to measure. What the exclusion owes in return (ADR-025) is shape '2c-ex' of the printed table — the same maximum RECORDED with the file charged — plus the equality pin GITHUB_API_MD_CHARS, and an arm asserting the unexcluded figure would NOT fit under this ceiling, so the exclusion is load-bearing rather than a rounding convenience. Re-derived by #360 as a measured 56_822 (shape '2c. PR-host spawn', post-review-summary: its PR-host body plus references/publication-gate.md) plus the RESERVATION LEDGER (2,050 ch since #360, PR2, spent its 150-ch line; one line per future PR of the SDLC-evidence series #357): PR3b 250 · PR4 900 · PR5 900. The reserved headroom is spoken for, not slack: each PR in the series spends only its own line, and any addition outside the ledger funds itself with a cut. git.md growth lands in this row too, so it reserves the whole ledger. Re-measure rather than trust a figure restated here: npm run build && npx vitest run tests/tracker/byte-budget.test.ts prints every row. May be LOWERED, never raised: condense the pr/ mechanics instead.

AC-2.5 [DR-13(a)] — max lines of the provider-resolution preamble, which is preloaded on every Git spawn. LOWERED 40 -> 36 on 2026-09-20 against a measured 35: the permitted direction, and the only direction this ceiling has ever moved in (a proposal to raise it to 70 was refused as strictly weaker than the assertion already in place). One line of headroom is deliberate — the next rule added to the preamble must retire one. May be LOWERED, never raised.

EC-17 — max characters of the Section-3 tracker directive TEMPLATE as spelled in src/assets/scripts/hooks/session-start-context. additionalContext is re-sent on every qualifying session start, so the directive length is a per-session cost. Measured 722 at the pin, headroom 78. Pinned against the hook SOURCE rather than the emitted text because the emitted text carries two absolute paths whose length is a property of the caller tmpdir, not of the directive. May be LOWERED after a pass that actually cuts the text, never raised: a cap raised to fit whatever the directive grew into is not a cap.

Max characters of the CLAUDE.md Tracker block — every consecutive bold-lead paragraph whose lead begins with Tracker, plus the blank lines between them. CLAUDE.md is loaded into every session in this repository, so the block length is a recurring per-session cost, and it is the paragraph run most likely to absorb every new tracker detail: a paragraph that grows a sentence per change has no natural stopping point. Measured 3,458 at the pin, headroom 42. May be LOWERED after a pass that cuts the text, never raised: a cap raised to fit whatever the block grew into is not a cap.
